title: MIPI HSI (High-Speed Synchronous Interface) link endpoint, frame mode

fields.desc: bit time - 1 in PCLK (3 or more on both ends)
channel bits per frame (0..4; larger values count as 4)

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: Frame to send; writing TX_DATA commits it. The core sends it once the peer's READY is high

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Received frame (head of the core's 4-frame FIFO); reading RX_DATA pops it

fdesc.rxq_ch: channel (upper bits 0 when fewer channel bits are used)

fields.desc: send a break (once the transmitter is idle; does not wait for READY)
a frame or break is being sent, or a break is pending

irqs.name: TX_SENT
irqs.desc: a frame was sent (TX_DONE is set earlier, when the core takes the frame)

irqs.name: ERR_OVERFLOW
irqs.desc: a frame arrived with the receive FIFO full and was dropped

irqs.name: ERR_STRAY
irqs.desc: a start bit followed fewer zeros than a break

irqs.name: ERR_DS
irqs.desc: DATA and FLAG changed in the same clock

irqs.name: ERR_TIMEOUT
irqs.desc: no bit for 4 bit times inside a frame (frame dropped)

notes: tx_data / tx_flag / tx_wake and tx_ready_in are the transmit lines (tx_ready_in is the peer's READY); rx_data / rx_flag / rx_wake and rx_ready_out are the receive lines. All pass through unchanged.
The receive lines are synchronised inside the core; the transmit lines are registered.
